title: Hydration mismatches and how to fix them

slides.text: When server and client must differ 🔀
slides.say: Hydration needs the first client render to match the server. But sometimes they just have to differ. You have two tools.

slides.text: Mismatches are bugs. At best they slow hydration down. At worst, event handlers get attached to the wrong elements.
slides.say: First, don't ignore mismatches. React recovers from some, but at worst event handlers get attached to the wrong elements.
Tool one. If one element's text or attribute unavoidably differs, like a date, add suppress hydration warning to it.

slides.text: It only works one level deep and is an escape hatch. React won't patch the mismatched text.
slides.say: It only works one level deep, and React won't patch the text. It's an escape hatch, so don't overuse it.
Tool two, two pass rendering. The first client render matches the server. Then an effect sets is client to true, and React renders again.

slides.text: Two passes mean rendering twice: slower hydration, and a UI that can jump after load.
slides.say: The cost: components render twice, so hydration is slower, and the UI can change suddenly after it loads.
